subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should OpenClaw replace the shipped `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` transcript archive convention and physical cleanup behavior with a permanent archive naming/directory model, and what migration or purge policy should existing users get?
rationale: Source inspection proves the current behavior, but choosing archive names, retained-transcript purge semantics, and migration behavior changes shipped filenames, config semantics, disk-budget behavior, docs, and downstream tooling expectations.

options.title: Adopt archive terminology with migration
options.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and keep physical purge behind an explicit documented retention setting.

options.title: Keep behavior and clarify docs
options.body: Leave current suffixes and cleanup behavior intact, but document that `.deleted.*` means detached until retention or disk-budget cleanup removes it.

options.title: Split terminology from purge policy
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/80263 for naming/config clarity and track the no-physical-delete policy as a separate durability decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt archive terminology with migration
recommendation.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and keep physical purge behind an explicit documented retention setting.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent archive-retention and disk-budget work makes this the best technical owner signal for the cleanup and purge-policy side of the decision.
